text:
Situation: Oxytocin is no longer on FDA's shortage list as of 2026-10-21. Current inventory at Corvale East and Corvale General provides 7.6 to 16.5 days of supply across four presentations.

Why (FDA record): FDA's shortage history shows oxytocin was first posted on 2022-09-23 and is now resolved as of 2026-10-21. An FDA inspection of Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC (FEI 1450022) ended 2022-06-30 and was classified OAI, with the classification letter dated 2024-04-30, 85 days before the shortage posting. A prior inspection of the same plant ended 2020-05-18 and was also classified OAI, with the letter dated 2024-05-22, 858 days before the posting. Later inspections of that plant in 2023-08-24 and 2023-10-13 were classified VAI, occurring 335 and 385 days after the posting. A second Fresenius Kabi plant (FEI 3001833549) received OAI classifications in 2011-07-08 and 2013-01-11, with letters dated 2017-12-28 and 2013-04-11, respectively.

Our position: Supply remains tight but the shortage is resolved per FDA. Two alternative manufacturers are approved and available. We will maintain current allocations and monitor daily usage.

Recommended actions:
1. Continue dispensing oxytocin 10 units/mL from Par Health USA, LLC as the preferred alternative; requires pharmacist verification for dose recalculation. Approved by Sam Rivera, MD on 2026-04-16. (Approver: Pharmacy Director)
2. Maintain oxytocin 10 USP units/mL from Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC as a secondary alternative; requires pharmacist verification for dose recalculation. Approved by Riley Brooks, PharmD on 2026-01-24. (Approver: Pharmacy Director)
3. Evaluate purchase from West-Ward Pharmaceuticals Corp if inventory falls below 5 days at any site; product is not on FDA's shortage list today. (Approver: Chief Pharmacy Buyer and Pharmacy Director)

Not recommended: No changes to current oxytocin protocols or dosing guidelines at this time. Clinical decisions remain with treating clinicians and the committee.
